title: PUAKILLER Benign Corpus
description: Machine-readable corpus of legitimate software, process names and publishers that no rule may ever match. Mirrors the corpora inside tests/Test-PuaRules.ps1, which remain authoritative; tests/Test-RuleCatalog.ps1 fails if the two drift apart. This file exists so the intel factory can check a candidate for benign collisions without parsing PowerShell.

names.description: Application, folder and file names that must never be flagged, and must never equal a rule's Name. Deliberately includes decoys that collide with real PUA aliases: 'OB', 'Shift', 'PDF Editor', 'Recipe Setup.exe'.

processes.description: Legitimate and OS process names that must never appear in any rule's Proc kill list.

publishers.description: Legitimate signing publishers that must never match the abused-signer alternation. Includes near misses of real blocked signers, such as 'Work Product Solutions LLC' and 'Shift Technologies Inc.'.
